primitives.name: Attention Modulation Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Bearing the limitations of eye tracking as a simple direct control input in mind, in this paper, we propose to use it to control the attention of the player's avatar and the game's procedural content generation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A(t)': 'Avatar attention state at time t (dimensionless)', 'G(t)': 'Player gaze vector at time t (normalized 2D vector)', 'P(A|G)': 'Conditional probability of avatar attention given gaze (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Avatar attention follows a probabilistic mapping from player gaze; gaze data is temporally synchronized with game events.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When gaze fixation duration < 100ms or spatial variance > 0.5 radians, kernel becomes non-invertible.

layer2.mapping: Player gaze vector G(t) is isomorphically mapped to avatar attention state A(t) through P(A|G), enabling real-time attention-driven procedural content adaptation.
layer2.telemetry: Average deviation of avatar focus from gaze direction over 10s intervals

primitives.name: Procedural Content Adaptation
primitives.verbatim_quote: This use of eye tracking is focused in mapping the player's and avatar's attention processes, which we believe to be much more natural and useful than allowing the player to directly control a pointer with the eyes, which has no actual mapping to real life.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(t)': 'Spawn probability of obstacle at time t (dimensionless)', 'A(t)': 'Avatar attention state at time t (dimensionless)', 'F(S|A)': 'Conditional frequency of obstacle spawn given attention (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Obstacle spawn rate is a monotonically increasing function of avatar attention concentration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A(t) < 0.2, S(t) approaches baseline spawn rate; when A(t) > 0.8, S(t) exceeds threshold.

layer2.mapping: Adaptive spawn rate S(t) derived from attention kernel A(t) via F(S|A), creating dynamic difficulty scaling.
layer2.telemetry: Observed spawn density vs predicted density under attention model

primitives.name: Immersive Experience Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Evaluation sessions showed that the proposed use of eye tracking provides a more challenging and immersive experience to the player, when compared to its absence.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I(t)': 'Immersive experience index at time t (dimensionless)', 'E(t)': 'Engagement level at time t (dimensionless)', 'T(t)': 'Task load at time t (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Immersiveness increases with engagement and decreases with task load; E(t) and T(t) are derived from gaze and action logs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T(t) > 0.7, I(t) plateaus due to cognitive overload.

layer2.mapping: I(t) = f(E(t), T(t)) where f is a sigmoidal function capturing the balance between engagement and task complexity.
layer2.telemetry: Subjective immersion score averaged across 5-minute intervals during gameplay

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that eye tracking should not replace traditional input but enhance gameplay through attention modeling. The attention modulation kernel maps player gaze to avatar focus, creating a dual process: one where the player’s visual attention guides the game world, and another where the game reacts to that attention. This leads to a derived kernel for procedural content adaptation, where obstacle spawns correlate with avatar attention levels. The immersive experience metric then quantifies how well this attention-guided system enhances player engagement. Failure modes include calibration drift, which introduces noise into the gaze signal, and low attention variance, which reduces the effectiveness of adaptive systems. These insights form a closed-loop system where gaze → attention → content → feedback → experience.
